m.pickBaseSame: Choose a knowledge base — the same one the learning module on the page uses.

revision.label: Revision
revision.use: A revision from a knowledge base (Cogita). Visible to those who can read the base — in a public area (open base) to everyone, without an account; progress without an account stays in the browser. Answers go to the area you choose (e.g. a course) — its leader sees the progress.
revision.missingRevision: Choose a revision from this knowledge base.
revision.showsTall: The whole revision at once — card by card.
revision.showsStrip: Heading and button — the revision opens on click.
revision.showsBlock: How many cards and how many you already know — a “Start” button.

flow.label: Course / story
flow.use: A flow from a knowledge base (Cogita): a course, a story, a conversation in bubbles, a map to explore. Visible to those who can read the base — in a public area to everyone, without an account.
flow.exTitle: A journey through the Gospel of Mark
flow.missingFlow: Choose a flow from this knowledge base.
flow.showsTall: The whole flow at once, step by step.
flow.showsStrip: Heading and button — the flow opens on click.
flow.showsBlock: What kind of flow it is, how many steps and goals — a “Start” button (or “Back to where you left off”).

live.label: Join a session
live.use: A field for a Cogita session code (live quiz, group revision, game) — a link with a QR code opens the session on this page right away.
live.showsStrip: One line: a code field and “Join”.
live.showsTall: A code field with an explanation — after joining, the whole session in the tile.
live.showsBlock: A code field and “Join” — after joining, questions and answers in the tile.

card.label: Entry card
card.use: One entry of a knowledge base — a person, a place, a concept, a piece of knowledge — with fields and a picture. Visible to those who can read the base.
card.showsStrip: One line: the entry’s name and its kind.
card.showsTall: The whole entry: all fields and files.
card.showsBlock: Name, picture and the first four fields.

table.label: Table of entries
table.use: Entries of a knowledge base as a table — with search; a small tile shows a list. Visible to those who can read the base.
table.retired: replaced by the “View” module (table). add a “View” module to the page and remove this one
table.kindHint: name of the kind, e.g. Person — empty: all
table.columnsHint: field names separated by commas — empty: the first four
table.showsStrip: One line: how many entries, a “See” button.
table.showsTall: The whole table with search; a clicked entry opens below it.
table.showsBlock: The first eight names — the rest in full screen.

topics.label: Topics
topics.use: Formerly: topics of a knowledge base. Topics no longer exist — the module only shows a notice; order comes from the “View” module with axes (kinds).
topics.retired: topics no longer exist — replaced by the “View” module (tree or matrix by axes: your own kinds, e.g. Mystery × Area). add a “View” module to the page and remove this one
topics.showsStrip: One line: how many topics, a “Browse” button.
topics.showsTall: Topics to go deeper into and the entries of the chosen topic.
topics.showsBlock: Topics as buttons — deeper on click.

map.label: Knowledge map
map.use: The entries of a revision as a map: what you already know is bright; the border to discover; the rest in the fog. Visible to those who can read the base (public area: everyone, without an account).
map.retired: replaced by the “View” module (map). add a “View” module to the page and remove this one
map.showsStrip: One line: how much you already know, a “Map” button.
map.showsTall: The whole map with names; a clicked entry and “Learn this”.
map.showsBlock: A small map — names on hover; a clicked entry in short.

seat.label: Learning (person with a link)
seat.use: Revisions from the course’s knowledge base for a person with a link — their progress goes to the course (leaders see it in Progress).
seat.revisionHint: revision id — empty: all revisions of the knowledge base
seat.missingBase: Choose the course’s knowledge base — the person with the link must be able to read its area (a form role or sharing).
seat.showsStrip: Heading and button — learning opens on click.
seat.showsTall: How many are waiting, how many they already know, and revisions to choose from.
seat.showsBlock: How many are waiting now and revisions to choose from.

rewards.label: Points and streak
rewards.use: Points, streak of learning days, daily goal, level and badges of the person learning here — live: every answer in a learning module on this page adds points right away (“+10”), lights the streak flame, fills the daily goal. The rules (how many points for what, the goal, levels, badges) are the “Rewards” in the knowledge base (Learning → Rewards) — each page chooses its own.
rewards.showsStrip: One line: points, level, streak, daily goal, badges — after each answer “+10” above it.
rewards.showsTall: Everything: points with level, the streak flame with the last 28 days, the daily-goal ring, all badges and the latest rewards.
rewards.showsBlock: Points with level, the streak flame with the week, the daily-goal ring (whatever is ticked); a single chosen element — large.

stats.label: Live statistics
stats.use: Charts and numbers of the person learning here — they grow with every answer in a learning module on this page: points today answer by answer, points and the daily goal day by day, accuracy, streak; in the full view also where the cards are (what they know, what is fading).
stats.bitKnowledge: Where the cards are (in the full view)
stats.showsStrip: One line: today’s points, answers, accuracy and daily goal — live.
stats.showsTall: Numbers of the day, chart of today’s points, points and the daily goal day by day (7/14/30 days), where the cards are.
stats.showsBlock: Numbers of the day and the chart of today’s points — it grows with every answer.

landscape.label: Knowledge landscape
landscape.use: The knowledge landscape of a base (Cogita): “You” in the middle, around it fields of what you can learn now, further out mountains — the higher, the more is missing; what you know becomes land. Click a field: read, learn, revise, set a goal. Here the learner chooses how often questions come back — more often, standard, less often or “Once and done” (right once and finished) — unless the leader has set it for everyone in the base settings. Without a view — the whole base; with a view — only its entries; with several views the learner chooses above the map which landscape to look at. Clicking the house in the middle shows statistics and rewards, a double click — all at once. Visible to whoever can read the base.
landscape.titleHint: empty: name of the view or “Knowledge landscape”
landscape.viewsHint: empty: the whole base; several — the learner chooses
landscape.bitSpacing: Choice of “How often to ask” and “How many cards at once” (when the learner may change them)
landscape.bitLearner: Who is learning and where progress is kept
landscape.showsAsk: Above it the choice of how often to ask (if allowed).
landscape.showsStrip: Heading and button — the landscape opens on click.
landscape.showsTall: The whole landscape: zoom, rotate, fields with “Learn”, goal and paths.{ask}
landscape.showsTallSearch: The whole landscape: zoom, rotate, fields with “Learn”, goal and paths, search.{ask}
landscape.showsBlock: A small landscape — up to 24 fields; the rest in full screen.{ask}

settings.label: Learning settings
settings.use: Settings of the person learning here: how often questions come back — more often, standard, less often, “Once and done” (right once and finished) or your own intervals. Applies to all learning from this base (landscape, revisions, courses) — on other pages too. If the leader has set intervals for everyone (base settings), the module only shows what applies. Choose the same answers area as in the learning module on the page.
settings.answersHint: the same as in the learning module on this page — empty: as in the knowledge base
settings.showsStrip: One line: how often to ask now and “Change”.
settings.showsBlock: How often to ask — choose with one click, with a description; “Other…” sets the intervals exactly.
